long_biography.plain_text:
Trained as a mechanical engineer, Fraisse worked as a chemical salesman before starting a small packaging unit in 1981, when he was 25. The business became Rhône Chimie Industrie and then Fabrication Chimique Ardéchoise as it added chemical research, formulation and production. This vertical integration turned a local operation into a broader industrial manufacturer.

The group subsequently moved into household products and aerosols, followed by cosmetics and pharmaceutical production. Renamed Fareva in 2005, it expanded through acquired manufacturing sites in Europe and the Americas. Fraisse preserved private control and reinvestment capacity rather than taking private-equity capital, using that independence to pursue long-term customer contracts and international growth.
